content.value_statement: Unity DOTS can be difficult to apply safely across components, systems, jobs, and baking. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical ECS patterns for scalable game logic.
actual_capabilities: Explains ECS components, systems, entities, archetypes, chunks, and data layout tradeoffs.
Provides C# examples for ISystem, IJobEntity, EntityQuery, and Entity Command Buffers.
Shows patterns for Aspects, singleton components, baking, and native collections.
Summarizes performance practices for Burst, parallel jobs, chunk iteration, and structural changes.
Helps convert object-oriented Unity gameplay ideas into data-oriented ECS designs.
limitations: Does not run the Unity Editor, compile code, or validate package versions.
Examples require adaptation to each project architecture and Unity Entities version.
Does not replace profiling on target hardware for real performance decisions.
Covers common DOTS patterns, not every ECS feature or engine architecture choice.

use_cases.title: Create ECS Gameplay Foundations
use_cases.description: Define components, systems, and entity queries for movement, health, spawning, and game state.

use_cases.title: Optimize Large Entity Simulations
use_cases.description: Apply Burst, Jobs, native collections, and command buffers to improve CPU-bound gameplay systems.

use_cases.title: Migrate MonoBehaviour Code
use_cases.description: Translate object-oriented patterns into data-oriented ECS structures with authoring and baking workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic ECS Components
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Unity DOTS feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design ECS components for a Unity feature with movement, health, and team data. Explain each component and its data layout purpose.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Movement System
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate system implementation with Burst-friendly logic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Unity ECS movement system using ISystem and Burst. Include query design, job scheduling choices, and update order guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Convert MonoBehaviour Gameplay
prompt_templates.scenario: Migration from traditional Unity object code to DOTS.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this MonoBehaviour gameplay design into ECS components, systems, aspects, and baking steps. Note any managed data risks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Entity Simulation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance review for large entity counts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my ECS simulation plan for thousands of entities. Recommend Burst, Jobs, chunk iteration, command buffers, and profiling checks.

output_examples.input: I need enemies to move, take damage, and despawn when health reaches zero.
output_examples.output: A component model, system responsibilities, command buffer usage, and Burst-friendly update guidance.

output_examples.input: My spawning system slows down when many entities are created in one frame.
output_examples.output: A performance review that recommends batched structural changes, deferred playback, query limits, and profiling checks.

output_examples.input: I want to convert prefab authoring data into ECS entities.
output_examples.output: A baking workflow with authoring fields, entity conversion steps, dependency notes, and runtime component boundaries.

best_practices: Start with simple IComponentData types before adding aspects, buffers, or shared components.
Use ISystem, Burst, and parallel jobs for hot paths after behavior is clear.
Batch structural changes through Entity Command Buffers instead of changing entities inside tight loops.
anti_patterns: Do not store managed Unity objects in Burst-critical ECS components.
Do not add or remove components repeatedly inside hot gameplay loops.
Do not assume ECS improves every system without measuring real workload performance.

faq.question: What Unity work is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for DOTS gameplay systems that need scalable entity processing and clear data layout.

faq.question: Does it generate complete Unity projects?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns, explanations, and code guidance that users adapt inside their own projects.

faq.question: Can it help with Burst and Jobs?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Burst-friendly systems, job scheduling, native collections, and parallel processing patterns.

faq.question: Does it replace Unity profiling?
faq.answer: No. It recommends patterns, but real performance must be verified with Unity Profiler and target hardware.

faq.question: Can it help migrate MonoBehaviour code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can map object-oriented gameplay into ECS data, systems, aspects, and baking workflows.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
